'''''Lithops salicola''''' is a species of [[perennial]] [[plant]] in the family [[Aizoaceae]], often called '''living stones''',<ref name=africanplant>[http://www.ville-ge.ch/musinfo/bd/cjb/africa/details.php?langue=an&id=109520 African Plant Database]</ref> because of its resemblance to round grey pebbles.

==Description==
''Lithops salicola'' has two coupled leaves, divided by a fissure through which the flowers appear. It is cylindrical or conical with a flat surface and green-gray coloration. The flowers are white and very small.<ref name=flowstones>{{cite web|title=Lithops salicola L. Bol. (1936)|url=http://www.floweringstones.co.za/species/salicola.html|work=Lithops species|accessdate=19 January 2014}}</ref><ref name = iucn >[https://books.google.com/books?id=XIL9adYYeSIC&dq=lithops+salicola+namibia&pg=PA45 1997 IUCN red list of threatened plants]</ref> It grows to a height of {{convert|2 |cm|in|abbr=on}}.<ref name = africanplant />

==Distribution==
This species can be found in the [[Cape Provinces]] and [[Free State (province)|Free State]] of [[South Africa]]<ref name = powo>[https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:362486-1 ''Lithops salicola'' L.Bolus] ''[[Plants of the World Online]]''. Retrieved 29 September 2023.</ref> at an elevation of {{convert|1000|m|ft}} to {{convert|1350|m|ft}}. It is generally found in well-drained [[soil]] or in rock crevices. It occurs in an area of summer rainfall.

==Cultivation==
''L. salicola'' is commonly used as a [[houseplant]] or for landscaping. Like all ''[[Lithops]]'' species, it requires extremely well-drained soil. It also grows in annual cycles, as the leaf-pairs flower, and then each produces a new leaf-pair that replaces the old one (which shrivels away). The principal rule of watering is that plants should be kept dry from when they finish flowering, up until the old leaf-pairs are fully replaced.

Of the ''Lithops'' species, ''L. salicola'' is one of the species which is most tolerant of occasional incorrect watering, and therefore among the easiest to cultivate (together with ''[[Lithops lesliei|L. lesliei]]'', ''[[Lithops hookeri|L. hookeri]]'' and ''[[Lithops aucampiae|L. aucampiae]]'').<ref name=encly>{{cite encyclopedia|title=Lithops salicola C351 TL: 10 km W of Luckhoff, South Africa cv. Malachite|url=http://llifle.com/Encyclopedia/SUCCULENTS/Family/Aizoaceae/14160/Lithops_salicola_C351_TL:_10_km_W_of_Luckhoff,_South_Africa_cv._Malachite|encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of living forms|accessdate=19 January 2014}}</ref><ref name = iucn />

In the United Kingdom ''L. salicola'' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/150628/i-Lithops-salicola-i/Details | title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Lithops salicola'' | website = www.rhs.org 
| accessdate=25 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf
